meaning: The library index's list of papers, in the order the page shows them. Order: the significance of the result, with work by other researchers before Will Cook's companion writing, and his own research last. tier places an entry in a section (lead, research, companion, own); kind names what the reader opens; provenance and provenance_label name who produced or supported the result (the colour is secondary to the label); credits give each role separately; versions are the direct choices shown on the entry, the first being the main one. An entry with "library": true is built here from instances/<id>/ (or, with "artifact": true, exported into the library by its own repository) and is listed only once published; its title, authors and counts come from its instance and edition. Any other entry keeps its current site's fields, read from the files named in counted_from. film names a short video in site/src/app/family.json; the entry offers it as its last version, with its running time.

papers.sentence: Proves that there are smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free initial data on ℝ³, and smooth divergence-free data on the torus, whose solutions of the unforced three-dimensional Navier–Stokes equations blow up in finite time, with the profile obtained from a numerical certificate the authors will release.
credits: Anthropic. The authors thank Anthropic and say they used Claude models throughout the work.
Will Cook, with AI assistance. Every change is marked in the reader.

papers.sentence: Constructs smooth periodic initial data for the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations whose solution blows up in finite time, with the velocity bounded and the vorticity at the origin tending to infinity.
credits: Levent Alpöge, Tristan Buckmaster and Matei P. Coiculescu
Anthropic. The authors thank Anthropic for the collaboration.
Will Cook, with AI assistance. Changes are marked, and the estimates it adds are disclosed separately.

papers.title: Constant-query verification by algebraic encoding
authors: Will Cook, with AI assistance (explanatory reconstruction)
papers.sentence: The PCP theorem: every language in NP has a polynomial-time verifier with logarithmic randomness, constantly many proof-bit queries, perfect completeness and soundness error at most one half, by the algebraic proof of Amireddy, Behera, Srinivasan, Sudan and Willumsgaard.
papers.credit: Original algebraic proof by Amireddy, Behera, Srinivasan, Sudan and Willumsgaard. Lean formalization by Troy Lee.
papers.where: On its current site, Proof Reader.
papers.comparator: Comparator accepted the forward theorem, its converse and the equivalence with the reference NP class.
credits: Amireddy, Behera, Srinivasan, Sudan and Willumsgaard

papers.sentence: For every power below four there is a total Boolean function whose randomized query complexity exceeds that power of its quantum query complexity, and four is the best possible exponent. Three accounts of OpenAI’s proof, each linked phrase by phrase to the Lean, which checks the optimal exponent with no hypothesis.
papers.kind: Original paper · Companion reconstruction · New Lean
credits: Reconstruction, new Lean and three accounts
AI systems under Will Cook’s direction

papers.sentence: A minimising Parisi order parameter of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick spin glass has no gaps: it increases across every interval in [0, 1), and its derivative is positive between 0 and 1.
papers.kind: Companion papers on an existing Lean proof

papers.title: The minimum of the coupled spring potential
authors: AI agents under Will Cook’s direction (the page)
papers.sentence: The coupled spring potential U(x₀, x₁) = x₀² + x₀x₁ + x₁² has a local minimum at the origin, proved in PhyslibAlpha by a general second-derivative test.
papers.credit: Lean formalization by Bjørn Kjos-Hanssen, PhyslibAlpha in Physlib at be0a9ee.
papers.where: On its current site, Proof Reader.
papers.comparator: Comparator accepted the local-minimum theorem and rejected a control that asked for a local maximum.
papers.kind: Explanation of an existing Lean result

papers.sentence: Proves that the sum of 1/(2ᵃ − 1) over an infinite set A is irrational when A satisfies a weighted summability condition, has a summable divisor cover, or lies in a union of one set of each kind, at every integer base b ≥ 2; Erdős’s question for every infinite A stays open.
papers.comparator: Comparator accepted all 51 statements replayed on GitHub Actions.
credits: No independent mathematician has reviewed the papers

papers.title: Erdős #1041: Lemniscates and Newton flow
papers.sentence: Using ani’s degree-seven polynomial, Lean refutes the exact path-length statement of #1041 in Google DeepMind’s Formal Conjectures, and also checks positive trinomial and sharp collinear families. Review of how this matches Erdős’s 1958 wording is still pending.

papers.title: Erdős #243: Cubic-rate irrationality and reciprocal tails
papers.sentence: Proves that a strictly increasing integer sequence with a_n²/a_(n+1) = 1 + 3/n + o(n⁻³) has an irrational sum of reciprocals, and the same for every nonintegral regular rate above one, with Lean checks. The unrestricted Sylvester-tail question remains open.

papers.title: Erdős #249: Binary totient series
papers.sentence: Classifies the base-two totient-residue series for every positive modulus, checked in Lean, and gives the exact rank kᵉ+1 of the totient kernel at every base. The original series with unreduced totients remains open.

papers.title: Erdős #1049: Rational-base Lambert series
papers.sentence: Proves irrationality in Zudilin’s rational-base contour region, with exact Hankel orders, checked in Lean. Base 3/2 and the claim for every rational base remain open.

papers.title: Erdős #269: Three-prime running LCM
papers.sentence: Proves both two-prime running-LCM sums transcendental by an argument that uses a cited Hecke–Mahler theorem; Lean checks the formulas and the conditional transfer. The three-prime irrationality question remains open.

papers.title: Erdős #68: Factorial-denominator irrationality
papers.sentence: For S = ∑ 1/(n! − 1), shows that a denominator of S as a fraction would not divide 299999! and would exceed 10¹²⁰³⁸, and proves a 3/2 growth exponent for the common denominator in Lean. Irrationality itself is still unproved.

papers.title: Erdős #251: Prime-gap dyadic series
papers.sentence: Gives a synthetic prime-gap countermodel checked in Lean and a sparse-perturbation obstruction, which rule out some methods of proof. Neither concerns the actual prime gaps, and the question remains open.

papers.title: Reading eight Erdős problems together
papers.sentence: Connects the eight problems above. Its main theorems are ordinary proofs, and Lean checks the ingredients it names.
